author: 5kO0
content:
Implemented (this session). One-rule fix in escape_doc_text plus a regression test.

Code change in proto-blue-codegen/src/generator.rs::escape_doc_text:
  Inside the existing char-at-a-time loop, when ch == '\n', emit \"\\n/// \" instead of just '\\n'. The leading \"/// \" from each call site (`format!(\"/// {}\\n\", escape_doc_text(desc))`) provides the prefix for the first line; this new behaviour provides the continuation prefix for every subsequent line.

Multi-paragraph descriptions (blank line between) survive cleanly: \"Para one.\\n\\nPara two.\" → \"Para one.\\n/// \\n/// Para two.\" → renders as a paragraph break in rustdoc.

The pre-existing call site at line 478 (CallError variants) that does \`escape_doc_text(&desc.replace('\\n', \" \"))\` is unaffected: it intentionally flattens newlines BEFORE calling the helper, so there are none for the helper to insert continuations on.

Test added: escape_doc_text_inserts_continuation_on_newlines covers single-newline, multi-paragraph (with empty middle line), and plain-no-newlines passthrough.

Verification (rust-quality §honest reporting):
  cargo test -p proto-blue-codegen                                  PASS (20 tests; 1 new)
  cargo build --workspace                                           PASS
  cargo test --workspace                                            PASS (67 suites, 0 failures)
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings             PASS
  cargo fmt --all --check                                           PASS

Wild-corpus rustc-compile pass against the same 420-doc app+chat+com+tools slice that surfaced this bug: the parse error \"expected one of `!` or `::`, found keyword `for`\" at com/deckbelcher/richtext/mod.rs:42 is GONE. Spot-check confirms the lexicon's `\\n`-bearing description now emits as:

  /// A multi-block rich text document.
  /// Used for primers and other long-form content.

with both lines correctly `///`-prefixed.

Remaining test failures on that slice are unrelated:
  - 12 x E0433 cannot find community/org in crate — partial-corpus artifacts (cross-TLD refs to community.* / org.* not in the slice). Would resolve with a complete scrape.

Behavioural change: bundled corpus regeneration produced no semantic diff on the bundled bsky/atproto/chat/tools corpus (which contains no multi-line descriptions). Future regens against any third-party lexicon with newline-bearing descriptions will now compile rather than parse-error.

Category: A (root-cause) — fixed at the helper rather than at the 11 call sites that pre-process descriptions.
